target.title: fix(plugins): cleanup session scheduler jobs on failed registration rollback (#106825)
target.body:
Closes #106825

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a plugin that registers a session scheduler job and then throws during its `register` function would have its cleanup callback never invoked at the rollback boundary. The live session-scheduler record remained in module-global runtime state while the registry metadata was correctly restored — leaving external plugin-owned scheduler work (via `cleanup`) uncancelled after a failed registration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registration rollback (`createPluginRegistrationTransaction`) restores the registry snapshot and calls `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` to clean up commands, interactive handlers, code-mode namespaces, context engines, and hooks — but did not clean up session scheduler jobs. These jobs are stored in two layers: a `registry.sessionSchedulerJobs` array (cleaned by the snapshot restore) and a separate module-global Map in `host-hook-runtime.ts` (previously never cleaned on rollback).

The fix adds the existing `cleanupPluginSessionSchedulerJobs` call to the `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` function in `registry.ts`, filtered to the rolling-back plugin's records. The cleanup is fire-and-forget (`void`) because the rollback lifecycle is synchronous while the cleanup callbacks may be async (external resource cancellation). Any cleanup failures are logged as warnings via `pushDiagnostic`.

## User Impact

Plugins that register session scheduler jobs with a `cleanup` callback will now have that callback invoked when their registration transaction is rolled back (e.g., a later exception during the same `register` function). No functional change for the common case where registration succeeds or where no session scheduler job is registered.

## Evidence

**Focused regression test** — `plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts` (3 tests, all passing):

```
 ✓ plugins src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts (3 tests) 82ms
```

**Real-behavior proof script** (standalone `tsx` harness exercising production code paths — `createPluginRegistry` → `createPluginRegistrationTransaction` → `rollbackPluginGlobalSideEffects` → `cleanupPluginSessionSchedulerJobs`):

Before rollback: 1 live job, 1 registry entry
After rollback:
- cleanup callback calls: 1
- cleanup context: {"reason":"disable","sessionKey":"agent:main:main","jobId":"audit-job"}
- live jobs: [] (removed from module-global state)
- registry sessionSchedulerJobs: [] (restored by snapshot)

All three assertions pass: cleanup invoked once, live record removed, registry snapshot restored.

**Existing contract tests** — `scheduled-turns.contract.test.ts` (24 tests) and `run-context-lifecycle.contract.test.ts` (15 tests) both pass unaffected.

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using opencode with review by the author.

target.title: fix(slack): bound userCache growth with pruneMapToMaxSize

## What Problem This Solves

`userCache` in Slack monitor context stores resolved user names from successful `users.info` calls but had no pruning — every unique user ID accumulated forever. `channelCache` already bounds at 1024 via `pruneMapToMaxSize`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the current-main `channelCache` pattern for users: LRU touch on read, `pruneMapToMaxSize` on write, cap `SLACK_USER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 2048`, using `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`.

## User Impact

- Long-running Slack monitors no longer retain unbounded user-name cache entries.
- Active users stay resident (LRU touch); oldest entries evict first after the cap.

target.title: feat(discord): show subagent progress
target.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in Discord-scoped sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message, including count reactions, durable failure marker behavior, and typing keepalive while tracked work is active.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users currently have little visible feedback when an assistant turn delegates work to tracked sub-agents. Long-running turns can look idle after the initial message even though background sub-agents are still running, and a sub-agent failure is not visible on the original Discord message.

Discord also cannot represent concurrent work by adding the same emoji reaction multiple times from the same bot/user, so progress needs a count-based reaction model instead of repeated identical reactions.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Discord users get immediate, lightweight progress feedback during delegated work without waiting for the final assistant reply:

- `1️⃣`, `2️⃣`, etc. show the current active tracked sub-agent count for the turn
- the count reaction is replaced as the active count changes
- the count reaction disappears when no tracked sub-agents remain active
- `🔴` remains if any tracked sub-agent ends with a non-OK outcome
- typing stays active while tracked sub-agents are still running

Operators can configure the behavior with `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, including reaction progress, count emoji, failure emoji, typing keepalive, interval, and max-duration TTL.

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## Linked Context

No linked issues or external context were listed in the current PR body.

## What Changes

This PR adds Discord-scoped, best-effort sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message. The feature is opt-in with `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`.

When enabled:

- one configurable count reaction shows the number of currently active tracked sub-agents (`1️⃣` … `🔟` by default)
- count changes replace the previous count reaction instead of accumulating multiple ordinal reactions
- zero active tracked sub-agents removes the count reaction
- any non-OK completion leaves a durable configurable failure marker (`🔴` by default)
- Discord typing is kept alive independently while tracked sub-agents remain active, then stops when all tracked work finishes or the safety TTL expires

The implementation threads the source Discord message id through native `sessions_spawn`, tracked ACP spawn, requester origin metadata, and internal Discord progress hook handling so the Discord extension can target the correct parent message. Non-Discord callers and callers without a source message id keep existing behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds source/current message id propagation through delivery context and `sessions_spawn` tool context.
- Carries that id into native sub-agent spawn and tracked ACP registration.
- Keeps public plugin hook/requester metadata narrow while the Discord extension uses an internal Discord-only event shape for source-message progress targeting.
- Emits progress cleanup at run completion even when ordinary `subagent_ended` delivery is deferred.
- Adds a Discord progress tracker keyed by account id, parent channel id, typing/thread target id, and source message id to avoid thread collisions.
- Tracks active run ids and derives the displayed count from current active set size.
- Replaces the displayed count reaction when the active count changes, removes it at zero, and caps counts above the configured emoji list to the final configured emoji.
- Uses `unref` on typing timers where supported so keepalive intervals do not keep Node alive.
- Updates Discord config schema, exported config types, UI hints, generated channel config metadata, and docs.

## Tests / Verification

Focused validation and static/config/docs gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `20a11bf331429ed2fd521636910b4aa07c5dcc24`
- Current PR head: `0f0ea76085d4ddc271aa25bab129f9c518f95992`
- Re-squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.
- Removed invalid/unnecessary delivered-text visibility experiment from `d17f593b4d4428f6ba7318f55eb40d76c3932094`; legitimate Discord sub-agent progress behavior remains.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live Discord proof for source-message progress behavior, not only tests. The requested coverage was: count reaction add/replace/remove behavior, normal channel context, thread/forum context, concurrent tracked sub-agents, typing keepalive while tracked work is active, typing stop/drain and TTL behavior, and durable failure-marker behavior after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle.

The live proof below covers those requested behaviors: normal channel success, thread-bound success, concurrent count replacement/increment/decrement/clear, typing keepalive/stop plus TTL guard logs, and a durable failure marker retained on the original source message after non-OK lifecycle. Private host/path/token/session/network values are redacted; Discord IDs/timestamps shown are included only where they are needed to tie the proof to the source-message behavior.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Live Discord API proof was run from the installed PR stack on Dev-01 using `OpenClaw 2026.6.10-beta.1` at local HEAD `f15c88bd6f9 stack: combine beta memory slots and Discord progress`, with:

- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.reactions.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.typing.enabled=true`

Observed live behavior in Discord:

- **Normal channel success:** a Discord-originated parent turn spawned a tracked sub-agent run (`8c6dbfa0-e021-4c3a-9992-328de22caa13`). The source Discord message showed the active count reaction while the child was running, typing stayed active during child work, and the count reaction was removed after the child completed. Child proof line: `NORMAL_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:48:33Z`.
- **Thread-bound success:** a thread-bound Discord sub-agent run (`01fa6443-4fc1-409d-9cf3-969ce433edbd`) completed successfully while progress was shown from the Discord parent context. Child proof line: `THREAD_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:49:50Z`.
- **Concurrent count replacement:** two overlapping tracked sub-agent runs (`4b2701ef-85b0-41d5-a87f-f72924e21869` and `9a5b1e70-5b3b-4820-bb5f-cb6cb7b2a926`) exercised count add/replace/remove behavior. The Discord source message count reaction incremented while both children were active, decremented as the first child completed, and cleared after the second child completed. Child proof lines: `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_2_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:23Z` and `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_3_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:36Z`.
- **Typing keepalive/stop:** Discord typing was visible while tracked sub-agents were active and stopped after tracked work drained. Earlier long-running proof passes also hit the configured typing safety TTL, with gateway logs showing `[typing] TTL exceeded (60000ms), auto-stopping typing indicator`, confirming the timeout guard executes.

Additional observation: after the final child drains, there can be a brief visual gap before the parent posts its final reconciliation response. That appears to be parent-yield lifecycle behavior rather than this PR's sub-agent progress tracker; it is being tracked separately as a follow-up investigation and is not treated as a blocker for this PR.

Additional durable failure-marker proof was captured from a real Discord source message after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle:

- **Failure marker:** source message `1518528276031602788` in Discord channel `1507934992699756645` retained the configured durable failure reaction `🔴` with count `1` and `me: true` after the non-OK sub-agent lifecycle. The source message timestamp was `2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z`. A later follow-up heartbeat at `2026-06-22T08:29:48.355Z` reported a separate verification pass, confirming the red marker was left on the original source message rather than being ordinary final text delivery.

Redacted observation:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "1507934992699756645",
  "message_id": "1518528276031602788",
  "timestampUtc": "2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z",
  "content": "Extensively check over the branch end-to-end against the recommended fix and prior investigation/research to ensure everything is clean, finalized, and polished.",
  "reactions": [
    {
      "emoji": { "name": "🔴" },
      "count": 1,
      "me": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Compatibility and Risk

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

Tests: 11 files, +1232 / -20

target.title: fix(release): keep frozen package inventory self-contained
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Trusted-main release recovery failed while packaging a frozen stable target because the current packer imported a current-main inventory helper that does not exist in the frozen checkout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run the frozen source checkout's own inventory writer while loading `tsx` from trusted main. This keeps the target's inventory schema and dependencies self-contained without requiring new helper files to exist on older refs.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(tools-manager): use BigInt for lossless Content-Length comparison
target.body:
## Summary
Replace `Number()` + `isSafeInteger` with `BigInt()` for lossless Content-Length comparison in `downloadFile`.

## What Problem This Solves
`Number()` can lose precision when parsing large integer strings (≥16 digits). The existing `CONTENT_LENGTH_RE` regex `/^\d+$/` matches arbitrarily long digit strings with no upper bound, but `Number("9007199254740993")` returns `9007199254740992` — a different value.

Although `isSafeInteger` catches most precision-loss cases (any value that rounds above `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`), relying on `Number()` for integer comparison is fragile. A Content-Length string of 20+ digits like `"99999999999999999999"` becomes `100000000000000000000` through `Number()` — completely wrong.

In practice `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES` is 100 MB (~10⁸), so any oversized Content-Length is caught by the numeric comparison long before precision becomes an issue. This is a **correctness hardening** — using the right tool (`BigInt`) for integer comparison so the code is obviously correct at all scales.

**Code evidence**: in `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts:187-188`, the current code parses Content-Length through `Number()` which is not guaranteed lossless for arbitrary-length digit strings.

## Root Cause
The code was written using `Number()` for integer parsing, which is lossy for values beyond 2⁵³ − 1 (`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` = 9,007,199,254,740,991). The `isSafeInteger` guard partially mitigates this but:
1. It rejects values for the wrong reason (precision loss vs size cap)
2. The error message says "exceeds byte limit" when actually the value can't be accurately parsed
3. It relies on an indirect property (safe integer vs range check) rather than comparing the value directly

## Why This Fix
**Chosen approach**: `BigInt(contentLength) > BigInt(maxBytes)` — one-line replacement.

- **Correct**: `BigInt` preserves the exact integer from any digit string
- **Simpler**: replaces two conditions (`!isSafeInteger || > maxBytes`) with one (`> maxBytes`)
- **Proven**: `BigInt` is already used elsewhere in the codebase (`src/infra/kysely-sync.ts` etc.)
- **Minimal**: 2 lines removed, 1 line added

Alternatives considered:
- String length pre-check: avoids the problem but is ad-hoc
- `BigInt` + fallback: unnecessary — `BigInt` is well-supported in Node 22

## User Impact
No user-visible change. The existing behavior was already correct for all practical Content-Length values (≤ a few GB). This fix hardens the code against theoretically large Content-Length headers and makes the intent clearer.

## Evidence
- **Before (Number() approach)**: `Number("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740992` (precision LOST). `Number("99999999999999999999")` → `100000000000000000000` (massively wrong). ❌ FAIL
- **After (BigInt() approach)**: `BigInt("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740993n` (exact). `BigInt("99999999999999999999")` → `99999999999999999999n` (exact). ✓ PASS

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (Number() approach — precision loss)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
============================================================
Content-Length precision loss demonstration
============================================================
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9007199254740991

--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
Content-Length header: "9007199254740993"
Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
Actual BigInt value : 9007199254740993
Precision preserved?  : NO — LOST!

Old code (Number + isSafeInteger):
  declaredBytes = Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
  isSafeInteger(9007199254740992) = false
  => REJECT (declaredBytes=9007199254740992, reason="exceeds cap or not safe integer")

--- Case 3: 20-digit Content-Length ---
Number("99999999999999999999") = 100000000000000000000
Number result accurate?  NO — massively wrong!

FAIL: Number() lost precision on Content-Length '9007199254740993'
FAIL: Number() returned wrong value for 20-digit Content-Length
```

### After (BigInt() comparison — exact)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
New code (BigInt comparison):
  BigInt("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740993n
  9007199254740993n > 10n = true
  => REJECT (reason="exceeds cap")

--- Case 2: Normal Content-Length (within safe range) ---
Old: ACCEPT  |  New: ACCEPT

PASS: BigInt() preserves exact value: 9007199254740993n
```

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check` passed
- `vitest run src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` — 18 tests passed (2 new: large Content-Length rejection)
- Added regression test: "rejects downloads with large Content-Length that would lose precision with Number()"

target.title: fix(agents): bound compaction planning worker payloads
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the compaction planning and worker handoff paths, checked duplicate/open PR state for #100635, and independently reviewed and validated the branch locally.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #100635.

Compaction planning sanitizes private fields before worker handoff, but previously still sent full model-visible tool-result text and base64 image data through `workerData`. Large browser/command results or multimodal transcripts could therefore force multi-megabyte structured-clone work before summary-prompt truncation had a chance to help.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a planning-only projection before worker handoff:

- oversized tool-result text/content keeps a bounded UTF-16-safe sample plus omitted-character accounting;
- image blocks in user, custom, and tool-result content keep type/MIME metadata but omit base64 bytes;
- token-pressure accounting remains conservative, so chunking and pruning decisions still reflect the original payload;
- local fallback behavior and private-field sanitization remain unchanged.

Image bytes are not used by compaction's text serializer, while image token pressure is a fixed per-block estimate. Omitting only `data` therefore reduces worker cloning without changing summary text or planning pressure. The projection helper is split from worker orchestration so both implementation files stay within the repository LOC guard.

## User Impact

Long or multimodal sessions should spend less time and memory cloning redundant payloads into the compaction planning worker, reducing event-loop stall and OOM risk without changing compaction decisions or generated summary text.

## Evidence

Final rebase:

- `upstream/main`: `d361b4ccb85`
- branch head: `83d56d3c91e`

Validation:

target.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a restricted agent could create a recurring cron job with a trigger script and a `systemEvent` payload, then have that script receive the full coding tool surface. Main-session cron jobs require `systemEvent`, so the common path bypassed the creator's tool policy whenever cron triggers were enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator tool cap now applies whenever a cron job has a trigger script, in addition to isolated `agentTurn` jobs. The cap is retained on every cron payload shape, survives updates, is persisted through the cron SQLite store so it survives a gateway restart, and is passed to the headless trigger evaluator. This keeps the existing agent-turn behavior while covering main-session system events and command payloads.

Distinct from #12736, which concerns global cron deny policy; #97317 and #101349, which concern isolated agent-turn defaults; and #41484, which concerns elevated execution scope.

## User Impact

Agents restricted to a small tool set can use cron triggers without acquiring shell, exec, or patch capabilities beyond that set. Existing unrestricted operator-created cron jobs continue to work with their configured policy.

## Rebase onto current main

This branch was rebased onto current `main`. Three things needed re-expressing against main's current code, none of which change the fix:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` conflicted because `main` replaced `Type.Object({...}, { additionalProperties: false })` with the `closedObject()` helper. The cap fields were re-expressed in that helper form.
- The changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet that landed on `main` in #106387 forbids an already-oversized file from growing. `src/cron/service/jobs.ts`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` are all over the limit, so the cap additions tripped the gate. Cohesive declarations were hoisted into three companion leaf modules, mirroring the existing sibling convention: `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.types.ts` (type-only), `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.types.ts` (type-only wire types), and `src/cron/service/payload-merge.ts` (the cron payload merge rules the patch touches). All three source files are now back at or below their baseline line counts and the ratchet passes.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` now uses the repo's `expectDefined` helper for indexed job access, which main's tightened unchecked index access requires.

## Evidence

- The touched suites were re-run after the rebase with `node scripts/test-projects.mjs` and all pass: 145 checks in `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`, 199 checks across `src/cron/normalize.test.ts`, `src/cron/store.test.ts`, `src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts` and `src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts`, and 23 checks in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/cron-validators.test.ts`. 367 checks total.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` restart-aware round-trip coverage for the `systemEvent` and `command` tool caps; both fail on the pre-persistence codec and pass here.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` both pass, `node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` passes, and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files is clean.
- An earlier restart cap-loss and reload proof, pinned to a previous head, is in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104430#issuecomment-4945702410

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A cron trigger script created by a restricted caller must not receive tools the caller cannot use; a `systemEvent` main-session job with a trigger script previously kept no tool cap.
Real environment tested: The production `createCronTool` entry point (`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts`) driven via `tool.execute("add", ...)` on pristine main `1708faf85b` and on PR head `c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b` with the identical restricted creator (`creatorToolAllowlist: ["read", "cron"]`) creating a trigger-script `systemEvent` job; only the gateway RPC boundary was replaced to capture the params the tool sends.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PROOF_OUT=/tmp/proof-after.txt node_modules/.bin/tsx cron-trigger-proof.ts` (harness invokes the real cron tool `add` with `trigger.script` + `payload.kind=systemEvent`, prints the captured `cron.add` payload)
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 1708faf85b, identical restricted-caller input)
{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed"}
# AFTER (this patch, head c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b, identical input)
{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed","toolsAllow":["read","cron"]}
```
Observed result after fix: The persisted trigger-script job carries `toolsAllow: ["read","cron"]`, capping the trigger to exactly the creator-visible tools instead of receiving the full coding tool surface.
What was not tested: No live gateway tick with a provider-backed trigger evaluation, and the full build was not run.

target.title: fix: prevent completed Codex hook relays from lingering
target.body:
Closes #106838

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running native Codex hooks could leave completed OpenClaw relay CLI processes alive when CLI setup or a handler retained a referenced Node handle. Repeated parallel hook events could therefore accumulate process trees and memory after their relay work had finished.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hidden `hooks relay` command now uses the existing deferred one-shot shutdown path after its handler returns. The shared wrapper propagates the relay's numeric exit code, lets `runCli` complete normal harness, proxy, memory, and stdin teardown, and drains stdout and stderr before exiting. This does not change the native relay protocol, gateway behavior, configuration, or external timeout handling before a relay handler completes.

## User Impact

Completed native Codex hook relays now terminate even when a referenced Node handle would otherwise keep the CLI alive. This prevents completed relay processes from accumulating across parallel tool batches while preserving Codex-compatible output and exit statuses.

## Evidence

- Deterministic local process reproduction with a preload that creates a referenced `setInterval` and writes a marker proving it loaded:

target.title: fix(slack): add 30s timeout to directory client API calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createSlackDirectoryClient` creates a `WebClient` without an explicit request timeout. If the Slack API hangs (network issues, Slack service degradation), the calling thread blocks until the OS kills the TCP connection (~2 min+). In paginated operations like `users.list` and `conversations.list`, every page can hang independently.

## Changes

- `extensions/slack/src/directory-live.ts:21`: Pass `{ timeout: 30_000 }` to `createSlackWebClient`
- Covers all 4 API calls in this file: `auth.test`, `users.info`, `users.list` (paginated), `conversations.list` (paginated)
- Pattern identical to #105893 (Alix-007) and 50+ other merged timeout PRs

## Evidence

**Unit tests (7/7 passed):**
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

**Lint:** `npx oxlint` — no errors

**Type check:** `pnpm tsgo` — no errors

**Real behaviour proof (real Slack API timing + hostname + before/after):**
```
========================================================================
  PLATINUM PROOF — directory-live.ts timeout fix
  Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
  Date: 2026年 07月 14日 星期二 01:51:43 CST
========================================================================

=== API baseline timing (without fix) ===
--- auth.test ---
  HTTP 200 in 626ms
--- users.list ---
  HTTP 200 in 583ms
--- conversations.list ---

=== The Bug (no timeout) ===
createSlackWebClient() creates WebClient WITHOUT timeout:
  - @slack/web-api default timeout: NO TIMEOUT (waits indefinitely)

  - If Slack API hangs, JS thread blocks until OS kills TCP (~2 min+)
```

target.title: fix(agents): decouple MCP retirement from browser cleanup
target.body:
Related: #76233
Related: #101830

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a completed run-mode subagent waits for sequential browser-tab cleanup before retiring its bundle MCP runtime and starting completion delivery. A browser close request can wait up to the browser service timeout per tab, so one run with several tabs can delay MCP retirement, the completion announcement, and the next same-session turn.

The concrete sequential browser-cleanup delay is separate from the MCP lease-disposal race covered by #76233 and the related #101830 work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser cleanup is dispatched as independent owner-scoped work, while MCP retirement and completion announcement proceed after the existing generation and lease-safety checks. Browser operations hold a per-session access gate for their full request; cleanup takes the exclusive gate, so a successor browser turn waits safely instead of racing an already-issued close request.

The browser registry tracks the opaque run owner and an ordered ownership claim. Successor reuse transfers ownership; late predecessor callbacks cannot reclaim or remove the successor tab. Failed non-ignorable closes remain tracked for a later cleanup, and legacy unowned tabs remain eligible for cleanup.

`runId` remains an additive, optional Plugin SDK context field. It is host-issued, stable for the active run, opaque, and absent outside an active run. Plugins may use it only to key ephemeral plugin-owned resources and cleanup; they must not parse it, persist it as application data, expose it to users, or use it as an authentication or authorization boundary. The contract is documented in `docs/plugins/building-plugins.md` and covered at the `defineToolPlugin` factory boundary in `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`; the existing agent-context test covers runtime propagation.

## User Impact

Run-mode subagent completion no longer waits for the browser service to close every tracked tab before MCP retirement and completion delivery begin. A successor turn can start its non-browser work immediately and its browser work is admitted after the old cleanup gate releases, preserving tab safety. App-view MCP leases continue to defer retirement until their release path completes.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: keep yielded parent runs deferred until subagents settle
target.body:
## Summary

This change promotes yielded-parent semantics into a shared parent lifecycle classifier and routes the affected cron, subagent-registry, and Discord/source-message paths through that state instead of letting each consumer infer completion from terminal-shaped model-attempt events, missing final text, or abort-shaped control flow.

The shipped behavior is:

- yielded parent + active descendants is treated as waiting/deferred, not ordinary completion;
- yielded parent + no descendant is treated as diagnostic error;
- cron delivery waits for a real final outcome instead of counting the yielded attempt as `ok / not-delivered`;
- Discord/source-message progress remains parent-owned while the yielded parent is waiting;
- descendant settlement wakes/reconciles yielded parents through the existing continuation paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where parent-agent runs that spawned child sessions/subagents and then called `sessions_yield` could look finished before the parent task actually completed.

The most visible failures were:

- isolated cron `agentTurn` jobs with valid delivery targets could finish as `ok / not-delivered` because the yielded parent had no final payload yet;
- Discord source-message lifecycle could clear parent progress/done indicators while child work was still active or while the parent was waiting to reconcile final output;
- run history/status surfaces made yielded parent work look like delivery failure, ordinary success with no output, or completed source-message work instead of a paused/resumable parent lifecycle.

`session_yield` is supposed to end the current model turn, not the parent task. This PR makes that distinction explicit for the affected runtime consumers.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Operators and developers can now rely on `sessions_yield` after spawning child/subagent work without the parent run being misrepresented as complete at the cron or Discord lifecycle boundary.

Practically:

- autonomous development crons stop inflating misleading `ok / not-delivered` results for intentionally yielded runs;
- cron history exposes a distinct `deferred` state for yielded parent handoff;
- Discord progress no longer marks the parent source message done just because the parent yielded while children continue;
- yielded parent runs are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles;
- debugging points to the parent/child lifecycle state instead of falsely implying delivery target resolution failed.

## Linked Context

- #95535 — `sessions_yield` isolated cron resumption/delivery gap.
- #92369 — subagent orchestration in isolated cron sessions needs reliable spawn/wait/aggregate semantics.
- #92116 — `sessions_yield` completion delivered as passive context can break orchestration loops.
- #86537 — subagent terminal reconciliation can expire suspended final delivery.
- #86538 — session write-lock timeouts can block subagent delivery lanes.
- #95833 — subagent abort-settle/session-lock failure can break session continuation.
- #92460 — isolated cron completion delivery gap around final controller return.
- #95604 — Discord subagent progress visibility.
- #94153 — durable queued subagent completion announcements.
- #95847 — requester-consumed descendant completion accounting.

## What Changes

### Shared parent lifecycle state

- Adds `src/agents/agent-lifecycle-parent-state.ts`.
- Classifies lifecycle events with explicit yielded/waiting vs terminal semantics.
- Exports the classifier through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.
- Routes subagent registry and Discord source-message handling through the classifier instead of local `yielded && paused` inference.

### Cron lifecycle and delivery

- Adds first-class cron run status `deferred`.
- Classifies yielded descendant handoff before delivery-mode branching, so text, structured payloads, `delivery.mode: none`, source-satisfied delivery, and normal direct delivery all share the same semantics.
- Prevents duplicate/interim parent announcements while descendants are active.
- Records yielded-without-descendant as explicit error diagnostic.
- Keeps deferred manual task runs active rather than failing them.
- Disables one-shot deferred cron jobs after handoff to avoid retry loops.

### Persistence, protocol, CLI, and UI

- Extends run-log JSON/SQLite encoding and status filtering for `deferred`.
- Extends Gateway protocol schemas and cron server filters.
- Extends CLI status/wait typing and docs.
- Extends hook-visible status typing.
- Adds Control UI status/filter labels and generated locale fallbacks.

### Parent/subagent reconciliation

- Tracks yielded/paused parents that still have pending descendants.
- Marks yielded parents with `wakeOnDescendantSettle` so they are resumed/reconciled when descendant work settles.
- Handles child success/failure settlement through existing subagent lifecycle recovery paths.
- Adds regression coverage for yielded parents being reconciled after child failure so diagnostics can wake the parent.

### Discord/source-message lifecycle

- Projects lifecycle events from agent execution into reply/channel handling.
- Uses the shared classifier to identify yielded/waiting parent state.
- Preserves in-progress/progress representation for yielded parents with active children.
- Avoids prematurely marking Discord status reactions done or clearing draft/progress state when the parent yielded and remains waiting.

### Concurrent user-message semantics

`docs/tools/subagents.md` documents the selected policy: if a human sends another message while a requester is yielded, the new message starts a normal turn for the same requester session. OpenClaw keeps the yielded run visible as waiting on descendant completion rather than converting it into a stale final reply; when descendant completion arrives, the completion event is handed back to the requester for synthesis.

## Implementation Notes

Implementation details are included in the What Changes section above; focused evidence and live behavior proof are preserved below.

## Tests / Verification

Focused test coverage plus type, docs, and formatting gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `c163d18fa610687e7dfb8585f1fe8f30b0c4185d`
- Current PR head: `73cff6aa1b0a3ab5786fdfc3a96c98f575e7fcc8`

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live behavior proof for the yielded-parent/deferred lifecycle across the surfaces touched by this PR. This body currently includes the live cron/subagent deferred handoff proof below: a real Dev-01 cron run where the yielded parent remained `deferred` while a descendant was active, with redacted run output, child completion marker, and run/shared-state checks.

Remaining ClawSweeper-requested proof not present in this body yet:

- Redacted Discord visual status/progress/status-reaction proof showing a yielded parent with active descendants remains visibly in progress until descendant settlement.
- Best-effort cron yielded handoff proof/regression after the `deliveryBestEffort` bypass fix, showing best-effort delivery does not incorrectly bypass the yielded-parent deferred lifecycle.
- Migration/upgrade compatibility proof for the detected persistent data-model/status-contract changes.

Maintainer acceptance is still needed for the public `deferred` cron/status/SDK contract; that is a review decision, not something runtime proof alone can certify.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

target.title: fix(slack): mark connected status degraded without bot identity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Slack `auth.test` fails at boot, or `channels.slack.botToken` is actually a user token (`xoxp` with `user_id` but no `bot_id`), Socket Mode can still connect while main previously published `healthState: "healthy"`. Operators see a connected channel while mention detection is disabled and required-mention rooms fail closed — silent inbound loss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Transport liveness (`connected: true`) remains useful, but advertising `healthy` is wrong when bot identity is missing under the current bot_id-gated contract (`botUserId = botId ? authUserId : ""`). target.title: fix(commitments): reject calendar-invalid due timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inferred commitments could accept an impossible calendar date from model output. For example, `2026-04-31T17:00:00.000Z` was normalized into May and could persist a check-in for a date the model never validly expressed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Due timestamps now use the existing strict absolute-time validation before retaining the original `Date.parse` result, preserving current timezone behavior. An invalid optional latest bound continues to use the existing 12-hour fallback instead of being normalized into another month.

This PR was AI-assisted. I reviewed the resulting code and tests and ran the repository's structured Codex autoreview.

Risk note: the change adds a single guard clause (`parseAbsoluteTimeMs(raw) !== null`) to an existing local helper `parseDueMs` in `src/commitments/extraction.ts:256`, reusing an established strict parser (`src/cron/parse.ts:65`) that shipped in v2026.6.9. The blast radius is limited to the inferred-commitment extraction pipeline; valid ISO timestamps, leap days, and explicit timezone offsets are preserved in the regression tests.

## User Impact

Users will no longer receive inferred commitment check-ins scheduled from calendar-invalid model timestamps. Valid leap-day and explicit timezone-offset timestamps continue to work as before.

## Evidence

### Exact-head configured-model extraction, parsing, and persistence after review

I ran an uncommitted local proof harness from the public PR head. It used the production `buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt` and `parseCommitmentExtractionOutput`, the configured DeepSeek provider through `runEmbeddedAgent`, and the exact-head runtime queue, candidate validation, and commitment store. The validation control appended to the production prompt forced the model to return the three timestamp shapes under test; no candidate or persisted record was synthesized by the harness.

Command:

```
OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT=../openclaw-pr-106236-proof node --import tsx --no-warnings contrib/pr106236-exact-head-proof.mjs
```

Redacted output (configuration paths, prompt text, session ids, and credentials omitted):

```
[model-fetch] provider=deepseek model=deepseek-v4-pro status=200 contentType=text/event-stream
HEAD: 6e142f4360a05fa337985d51fdb3f1a4593ac34b
Configured model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
Runtime queue items processed: 3
Model candidates parsed: 3
MODEL proof:invalid-earliest: earliest=2027-04-31T17:00:00.000Z latest=2027-05-01T23:00:00.000Z
MODEL proof:invalid-latest: earliest=2027-04-30T17:00:00.000Z latest=2027-04-31T23:00:00.000Z
MODEL proof:valid-leap-offset: earliest=2028-02-29T09:00:00-08:00 latest=2028-02-29T12:00:00-08:00
Stored records: 2
STORE proof:invalid-latest: earliest=2027-04-30T17:00:00.000Z latest=2027-05-01T05:00:00.000Z windowHours=12
STORE proof:valid-leap-offset: earliest=2028-02-29T17:00:00.000Z latest=2028-02-29T20:00:00.000Z windowHours=3
VERDICT: PASS — invalid earliest rejected; invalid latest fell back to 12h; valid leap-day offset persisted.
```

The store was isolated under a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and removed after the run. This proves the configured-model output crossed the exact-head parse, validation, and persistence boundaries: the impossible earliest date produced no stored record, the impossible optional latest bound used the existing 12-hour fallback, and the valid leap-day offset preserved its instants.

### Negative control — pre-fix gate accepts impossible calendar dates (real source functions)

`node --import tsx` drove the real `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` from `src/cron/parse.ts` against the pre-fix `parseDueMs` logic (Date.parse only):

```
Input: 2026-04-31T17:00:00.000Z
Date.parse result: 1777654800000 (finite: true)
Date.parse builds: 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
parseAbsoluteTimeMs: null

Pre-fix gate:  Number.isFinite(parsed) only → ACCEPTED (BUG — normalized to May 1)
Post-fix gate: Number.isFinite(parsed) && parseAbsoluteTimeMs !== null → REJECTED (FIXED)
```

### Real-behavior proof — after fix (real `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` + new `parseDueMs` logic)

Full proof harness exercising the real `src/cron/parse.ts` strict parser at `node --import tsx`:

```
========================================================================
  REAL-BEHAVIOR PROOF — PR #106236

========================================================================

PART 1 — parseAbsoluteTimeMs (the strict guard) raw output

  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       parseAbsoluteTimeMs → null (REJECTED)

  [valid leap day (Feb 29, leap year)]   parseAbsoluteTimeMs → 1835438400000
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z
  [valid normal date]                    parseAbsoluteTimeMs → 1784106000…
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [valid date +08:00 offset]             parseAbsoluteTimeMs → 1784106000…
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z

PART 2 — BEFORE fix (old parseDueMs = Date.parse only)
  [invalid calendar date (Apr 31)]       ACCEPTED → 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       ACCEPTED → 2025-03-01T10:00:00.000Z
  [valid leap day (Feb 29, leap year)]   ACCEPTED → 2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z
  [valid normal date]                    ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [valid date +08:00 offset]             ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [undefined input]                      REJECTED (undefined)

  OLD totals: 5 accepted, 1 rejected

PART 3 — AFTER fix (new parseDueMs = Date.parse + strict parse)

  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       REJECTED (undefined)
  [valid leap day (Feb 29, leap year)]   ACCEPTED → 2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z
  [valid normal date]                    ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [valid date +08:00 offset]             ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [undefined input]                      REJECTED (undefined)

  NEW totals: 3 accepted, 3 rejected

VERDICT
  Apr 31 rejected BEFORE fix: NO ← BUG (Date.parse normalizes to May 1)
  Apr 31 rejected AFTER  fix: YES ✓
  Feb 29 (non-leap) rejected BEFORE: NO ← BUG (Date.parse normalizes to Mar 1)
  Feb 29 (non-leap) rejected AFTER : YES ✓
  Valid leap day still accepted: YES ✓
  Valid normal date still accepted: YES ✓

  → FIX WORKS: invalid calendar dates blocked, valid dates preserved.
```

### Automated tests

- Focused test file passes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commitments/extraction.test.ts` — 1 file, 8 tests all green.
- Negative control: pre-fix test assertion confirmed the invalid-date test fails without the guard.

### Formatting / static checks

- `oxfmt src/commitments/extraction.ts src/commitments/extraction.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Structured autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

### What was not tested

The full build, check, and test suites are covered by the fork PR CI run. The configured-provider proof above uses a clearly labeled validation control appended to the production extraction prompt so the model emits all three boundary values deterministically; it does not claim natural-language model behavior. An ordinary user turn through the Gateway and later heartbeat delivery were not exercised because this change is in candidate date validation before persistence.

target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.


## Node-host prompt parity (b0164f0fe8a, 2026-07-09)

Review found that the `host=node` `security=full`/`ask=off` fast path invoked `system.run` directly before prepare/approval registration, so a denylist STOP rule hard-denied server-side (`denylist-hit`) instead of raising the documented human allow-once prompt.

Fixed for prompt parity (recommended option):

- The direct fast path is taken only when the caller-visible effective denylist is **known empty**: the `openclaw.json` config layer is empty AND the node approvals-file denylist (fetched via `exec.approvals.node.get`) is known and empty. Fetch failures fail **closed** into the prepare path.
- On the prepare path, the effective denylist (config layer + node approvals-file layer) is evaluated caller-side; a hit forces a registered human approval request even at full/off, mirroring the gateway host: auto-review is excluded (human-only), and `allow-always` is downgraded to one-shot so no durable trust can be minted from a denylist hit.
- Non-matching commands with a configured denylist still auto-run (via the prepare path); setups with no denylist keep the direct fast path.

Focused tests added in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts`: config-layer hit registers an approval request (no direct denial), approvals-file hit registers an approval request, non-matching denylist auto-runs, known-empty denylist keeps the fast path, approvals fetch failure fails closed to prepare. `vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts --pool=forks` => 4 files, 146 tests passed; tsgo typecheck clean.

Honest proof status: production decision-function proof and the focused node-host approval-registration tests are in; a live gateway+node prompt -> allow-once -> runs-exactly-once capture is being prepared on a dedicated QA host and will be appended when complete.

Known residual (intentional, documented here): a denylist configured ONLY in the node machine's own local `openclaw.json` remains invisible to the gateway-side caller and still hard-denies server-side (fail-closed). The two operator surfaces this PR documents (`tools.exec.denylist` config layer and the exec-approvals file) now both get prompt parity on host=node.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where process-cleanup tests could fail with `kill ESRCH` when a child exited between the helper's liveness probe and its SIGKILL call.

Focused regression coverage simulates the liveness-check/SIGKILL race and verifies non-ESRCH errors still propagate.

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.36.2 to 4.37.0
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.37.0

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

v4.36.3

No user facing changes.

Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956

4.37.0 - 08 Jul 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.2 - 04 Jun 2026

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852

target.title: refactor(channels): migrate googlechat, imessage, and whatsapp group policy onto the scope tree
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

First channel batch of the group-policy scope normalization (stage 2). Google Chat, iMessage, and WhatsApp resolved group `requireMention`/tool policy through the older generic resolver with per-channel plumbing; this migrates them onto the canonical ScopeTree resolvers so every channel converges on one resolution model before the custom-walker channels (discord, telegram, msteams, …) migrate and their ~600 LOC of private walkers get deleted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Depends on #106819 (ScopeTree core resolver — this branch stacks on it). These three are pure delegates, so they prove the migration pattern at minimal risk. A shared `buildChannelGroupsScopeTree(cfg, channel, accountId)` builder was added to core because 13+ channels share the flat `groups` config shape (wildcard `"*"` → defaults node, exact keys → scopes); richer channels will ship their own builders. Account scoping stays core-owned via `resolveChannelGroups`, preserving the single-account empty-`groups:{}` fallback quirk.

## User Impact

None — behavior parity: exact-group hit, wildcard fallback, account-level groups overriding root, sender-scoped tool policy (explicit `messageProvider` matches the old resolver's default), and default `true`/`undefined` when nothing is configured. Each plugin's group-policy module ended smaller than before (17/40/40 lines vs 18/41/41).

## Evidence

- Testbox (Blacksmith): `pnpm test src/config/group-scope-tree.test.ts src/config/group-policy.test.ts extensions/googlechat extensions/imessage extensions/whatsapp` all green; `check:changed` lanes green with the regenerated Plugin SDK API baseline hash committed.

target.title: fix(dreaming): drop heartbeat assistant responses from dream corpus
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The dreaming ingestion pipeline filters heartbeat **user** messages (containing `[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]`) via `sanitizeSessionText`, but the paired **assistant** response was only dropped when it was the exact string `HEARTBEAT_OK`. Local models frequently respond with natural-language acknowledgments (e.g. "Heartbeat received. Main is active.") which pass through the sanitizer unchanged and enter the dream corpus as low-confidence memory snippets.

See issue #103720.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original text-based heartbeat detection was user-spoofable (anyone could type the heartbeat marker and trigger the drop). The fix uses **runtime provenance** (`provenance: { kind: "heartbeat" }`) attached at the source in `get-reply-run.ts`, which cannot be spoofed by user input.

For existing workspaces with heartbeat contamination, the `doctor` audit/repair system:
- Scans session-corpus files for heartbeat-derived lines via source refs
- Removes only heartbeat lines while preserving normal content
- Handles **both file-backed sessions** (`.jsonl` paths) and **SQLite-backed sessions** (logical paths without extension) via a fallback to `loadTranscriptEventsSync`
- Avoids clearing session ingestion checkpoints to prevent corpus duplication on re-ingestion
- Falls through to self-ingestion narrative content checks even when heartbeat contamination is found

## User Impact

- **No visible change** for users without heartbeat contamination
- **Lower memory noise** for users with heartbeat-enabled sessions — average 0.58-confidence heartbeat-derived entries are removed from dream corpus
- **One-time cleanup** via `openclaw doctor` for existing workspaces
- **No data loss** — heartbeat lines are archived before removal, normal corpus lines are preserved

## Evidence

### Forward Prevention (Provenance-based)
- Heartbeat turns carry `provenance: { kind: "heartbeat" }` attached at the source in `get-reply-run.ts`
- `buildSessionEntry` checks `message.provenance.kind === "heartbeat"` instead of text-matching user content
- When a heartbeat user message is filtered, the immediately following assistant response is also dropped via a `pendingHeartbeatUserDrop` flag
- Cross-message coupling is gated by runtime provenance (not user-spoofable text per PR #70737)

### Backward Repair (Targeted Doctor Audit)
- `auditDreamingArtifacts` + `repairDreamingArtifacts` functions available via `openclaw doctor`
- Detects and archives heartbeat-derived session-corpus entries, contaminated session-ingestion state, and duplicate diary entries
- Handles both file-backed and SQLite logical session paths in corpus references

### Validation
- [x] Format: `oxfmt --check` passes
- [x] Lint: `oxlint --deny curly` passes
- [x] Extension tests: 63 files, 1046/1046 tests pass
- [x] Type check: `tsgo` passes

- [x] Autoreview: 2 P1s fixed (checkpoint clearing, path resolution), 2 remaining known issues in pre-existing code

| `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.ts` | `pendingHeartbeatUserDrop` flag + provenance-based heartbeat detection |

target.title: fix(sandbox): pin LC_ALL=C for sandbox stat on localized hosts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`SandboxFsBridge.stat()` decides whether a path is missing by matching the sandbox `stat` command's stderr against the English string `"No such file or directory"` (`src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.ts`). On a host whose shell/libc runs in a non-English locale, `stat` emits a translated ENOENT message, so an absent file falls through to `throw` instead of returning `null`. The same locale sensitivity hits the success path: `%F` prints a translated type word (e.g. `répertoire`), and `coerceStatType()` only recognizes the English `"directory"`, so a directory is misclassified as `"other"`. (Reported in #106576.)

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix is at the root: `buildStatPlan()` now runs the probe as `LC_ALL=C stat -c "%F|%s|%y" …`. Pinning `LC_ALL=C` for that one command forces both the ENOENT stderr and the `%F` type word to their fixed English forms that the caller already matches, instead of adding locale-specific string tables or a second `test -e` round-trip. It also stabilizes the `%y` mtime formatting the caller parses. `LC_ALL=C` is a plain per-command env assignment: corrective on glibc hosts and a harmless no-op on BusyBox/Alpine, so no backend regresses.

## User Impact

Sandbox filesystem `stat` (existence checks, type detection) now behaves identically regardless of the host locale. Missing files return `null` rather than throwing, and directories are typed correctly, on localized hosts.

## Evidence

- New focused regression in `src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts` asserts the stat plan emits `LC_ALL=C stat -c`; full file green (9 passed) via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.shell.test.ts`. Without the fix the assertion fails (script was `stat -c` with no locale pin).
- `git diff --check` clean; change is 2 files, +12/−1; no `CHANGELOG.md` edit.
- Source-reproducible: the behavior is a fixed English-string match against locale-dependent `stat` output; a live localized host is not required to demonstrate the defect or the fix.

Fixes #106576

target.title: fix(retry): recognize provider-wrapped transient 5xx for session retry
target.body:
Closes #106824

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with OpenAI Responses, Azure OpenAI Responses, or Mistral providers would not get session auto-retry for transient 5xx errors (500/502/503/504). The built-in provider adapters format these errors as `OpenAI API error (500): ...`, but the retry classifier only recognized HTTP status codes at the very beginning of the message — so a transient provider failure would terminate the turn immediately instead of scheduling the normal same-model retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status extractor `extractLeadingHttpStatus` intentionally reads status only from the start of the error string, a hardening introduced in #105258 to prevent arbitrary numeric substrings (model IDs like `model-x-500-preview`, image dimensions) from accidentally triggering retries. However, the repository's own provider adapters — OpenAI Responses (`openai-responses.ts:56`), Azure OpenAI Responses (`azure-openai-responses.ts:47`), and Mistral (`mistral.ts:287`) — all produce a parenthesized wrapper format `Provider API error (status): message` that the extractor does not recognize, and the fallback keyword patterns also do not match the typical OpenAI/Mistral error body text.

The fix adds a narrow anchored regex fallback at the call site in `isRetryableAssistantError` that recognizes only the three known repository-owned provider wrapper formats. It does not change `extractLeadingHttpStatus` (27 callers) or any shared helper module — the recognition scopes to the retry classifier alone, preserving the no-arbitrary-substring invariant from #105258.

## User Impact

Transient 500/502/503/504 responses from all three built-in adapters can schedule the normal session retry path again instead of failing the turn immediately. Permanent errors (4xx, quota exhaustion, model-not-found) remain correctly classified as non-retryable. Users with Azure OpenAI or Mistral providers also benefit from the fix, not just the primary OpenAI Responses surface.

## Evidence

**Unit tests** — 34/34 passing (21 existing + 13 new), no existing test modified:

target.title: fix(cron): drop plain-text format from announce delivery footer
target.body:
Closes #106430

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where isolated cron jobs with `delivery: announce` (and no message tool) append a footer that says **Return your response as plain text**, which some models (notably Qwen) obey by writing tool-like tags as plain text instead of making API-level tool calls. Other models ignore the instruction, so the bug is easy to miss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the format-constraining plain-text clause with neutral automatic-delivery guidance: **Your response will be delivered automatically.** This keeps the auto-delivery contract without telling models to suppress structured tool use.

Fix quality: compatibility — string-only prompt change on the non-message-tool announce path; no config/API/schema change. Performance — no hot-path cost. Usability — clearer delivery notice. Security — no trust-boundary change.

Note: open PR #106527 targets the same issue with a slightly different residual wording (`Return your response; …`). This PR follows ClawSweeper’s recommended neutral phrasing and drops the format instruction entirely.

## User Impact

Isolated announce cron runs can use non-message tools without a prompt footer that steers weaker models away from real tool calls. Automatic delivery of the final reply still works as before.

target.title: fix(reef): bound relay HTTP JSON response body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Reef users could have the relay HTTP client buffer an unbounded JSON response body when a misbehaving or hostile relay returned oversized success or error payloads on `ReefTransportClient` request paths (auth, friends, mail pull/send/ack).

Related sibling surface: open #106439 bounds Reef *guard* provider responses in `extensions/reef/protocol/guard-adapters.ts`; this PR covers the separate relay transport client in `extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`, which still used unbounded `response.json()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ReefTransportClient.request` now reads JSON through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`:

- success bodies capped at 16 MiB (`reef.relay`)
- error bodies capped at 64 KiB (`reef.relay.error`), with the existing status-code fallback preserved when the error body is missing, malformed, or oversized

Oversized streams are cancelled before the remainder is buffered. Non-goal: changing guard adapters (owned by #106439) or adding new config.

## User Impact

Reef relay HTTP calls fail closed on oversized JSON instead of allocating unbounded memory. Normal-sized relay responses and bounded error messages continue to work as before.

## Evidence

Head: `7d4ab0a3461a71021bd0d0ba53d5aade8573206f`

**Head:** `f8d35557ae69c3e457b601cbe2bc535049689032`

**Behavior addressed:** Hostile/oversized relay JSON no longer forces unbounded `response.json()` allocation; streams cancel after the byte budget.

**Real environment tested:** Linux WSL2, Node `v22.22.0`, local checkout of this branch.

```text
ok
```

target.title: fix(ai): record token usage on Responses early-abort (#100954)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Azure/OpenAI Responses streams that end early with `response.incomplete` (e.g. `max_output_tokens` reached, content filter) never send `response.completed`. Both Responses stream processors on `main` assign `output.usage` **only** inside the `response.completed` branch, so these early-terminated streams leave usage — and its cost — at zero, dropping the reported token counts (including partial cache-hit tokens) and their cost from telemetry and session accounting. This is the drift described in #100954.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `response.incomplete` event carries a full `Response` object with the same `usage` shape (`input_tokens` / `output_tokens` / `total_tokens` + `input_tokens_details`) as `response.completed`. The fix records that usage — **and computes its cost** — when the stream terminates early.

Two processors handle Responses streams and both had the identical completed-only defect, so both are fixed:
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts`
- `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts`

In each, the terminal usage+cost logic is extracted into a shared `recordResponsesTerminalUsage` helper (map usage → `calculateCost` → service-tier pricing) that both `response.completed` and the new `response.incomplete` branch call. Cost must run for the incomplete path too because session accounting sums `usage.cost.total` (`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`); recording tokens without cost would still under-report. Stop-reason mapping and completed-only backfill stay specific to `response.completed`. The abort lifecycle already forwards a populated `output.usage` into the emitted error event, so no changes to the abort path or the generic `normalizeUsage` were needed.

## User Impact

Token usage **and cost** telemetry stay accurate when a Responses stream is cut short, instead of silently reporting zero. No change to normal (`response.completed`) streams or to provider defaults.

## Evidence

Reproduction and after-fix behavior are exercised by regression tests that drive a real `response.incomplete` event (carrying nonzero tokens, including cache reads/writes) through the actual stream processors with **no** `response.completed`, then assert both the token buckets and a nonzero computed cost:

- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` → **35 passed** (new early-abort test asserts `usage.cost.total > 0` and exact per-bucket cost)
- `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` → **298 passed** (same regression added for the sibling processor)
- `src/agents/usage.normalization.test.ts` → **10 passed**
- Type check (`tsgo` core project) → clean

Note on live proof: a redacted real-Azure early-abort transcript would require forcing `max_output_tokens`/content-filter termination against a live deployment, which I can't capture here. The regression tests instead feed the exact SDK `response.incomplete` event shape (per the OpenAI Node `ResponseIncompleteEvent` → `Response.usage` contract) through the unmodified processors, so they exercise the real terminal code path rather than a mock.

Closes #100954

---
This is AI-assisted work.

target.title: fix(agents): terminate agent run on critical loop detection instead of continuing indefinitely
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Critical loop detection correctly blocks a stuck tool (`deniedReason: "tool-loop"`, `action=block`), but the blocked result was returned as an ordinary tool result. The agent kept issuing provider turns and re-calling the same tool for hours (#106231).

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper Rank-up on the previous abort-helper tip required the **canonical agent-core termination contracts** instead of `abortRun` at the embedded-run boundary (which records synthetic `stopReason: "aborted"` and can cancel sibling tools in mixed batches).

Dual-layer stop:

1. **Per-result** `terminate: true` on critical tool-loop blocked results → `shouldTerminateToolBatch` stops single/all-veto batches.
2. **Post-turn** `shouldStopAfterTurn` in `createAgentSession` → stops **mixed** batches when any finalized result has `deniedReason: "tool-loop"`.

Plugin / approval vetoes stay non-terminating.

## User Impact

- Critical tool loops terminate the agent run instead of burning tokens indefinitely.
- Mixed parallel batches complete non-loop tools, then stop before the next provider turn.
- Non-loop blocks unchanged.
- Terminal outcome follows normal loop completion (not a synthetic aborted assistant message from embedded `abortRun`).

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `59977a726886274d04a036be59c7392972d67db9` (rebuilt from current `main`; replaces prior `critical-tool-loop-abort` approach)

**Patch quality:** platinum-shaped — 6 files, +232/−1 net, single owner boundary, no speculative exports, clean compare vs main.

| Replace embedded abort with terminate + post-turn contracts | done |
| Cover single-tool + mixed-batch | done (`agent-loop.test.ts`, `blocked-result.test.ts`) |
